t: You're looking at 27 and 28 Berkeley Square, a building in Westminster. Daisy Greville, Countess of Warwick, was born here in 1861. She moved in late-Victorian high society, yet she became a campaigning socialist, and people called her the Red Countess. She backed schemes for education, housing, employment and pay, and she set up colleges for women in agriculture and market gardening, first in Reading, then in Studley. She was also a long-term confidante and mistress to the Prince of Wales.
